11. One Line of Working Code Is Worth 500 of Specification

作者：Allison Randal

Design is a beautiful thing. A systematic, detailed presentation and review of a problem space and solution reveals errors and opportunities for improvement, sometimes in a startlingly dramatic way. The specifications are important because they provide the pattern for building. Taking the time to think through the architecture is important, both on a macro level with an eye for interactions between components and, on a micro level with an eye for behavior within a component.

设计是一件美妙的事。对问题空间和方案做系统、细致的呈现与评审，能以惊人的方式暴露错误和改进机会。规格说明书很重要，因为它们提供了构建的蓝本。花时间把架构想透很重要——宏观上关注组件间交互，微观上关注组件内部行为。

Unfortunately it’s far too easy to get wrapped up in the process of design, enthralled by architecture in abstract. The fact is that specifications alone have no value. The ultimate goal of a software project is a production system. A software architect must always keep an eye on this goal, and remember that design is merely a means to an end, not an end in itself. An architect for a skyscraper who ignored the laws of physics to make the building more beautiful would soon regret it. Losing sight of the goal of working code spells serious trouble for any project.

不幸的是，我们太容易沉浸在设计过程里，被抽象的架构迷住。事实是，光有规格说明书毫无价值。软件项目的终极目标是一个能跑的生产系统。软件架构师必须始终盯着这个目标，记住设计只是达成目的的手段，而非目的本身。一个摩天大楼的架构师如果为了让建筑更美而无视物理定律，很快就会后悔。忘记「能跑的代码」这个目标，对任何项目都是大麻烦。

Value the team members who work on implementing your vision. Listen to them. When they have problems with the design, there’s a good chance they’re right and the design is wrong, or at least unclear. It’s your job, in these cases, to modify the design to meet real-world constraints by working with your team members to determine what works and what does not. No design is perfect from the start; all designs need to be modified as they are implemented.

重视那些动手实现你愿景的团队成员。倾听他们。当他们对设计有意见时，很可能他们是对的、设计错了，或者至少不清楚。这种情况下，你的工作是和团队一起搞清楚什么行得通、什么行不通，修改设计以贴合现实约束。没有设计一开始就是完美的；所有设计都要在实现过程中被修改。

If you’re also a developer on the project, value the time you spend writing code, and don’t believe anyone who tells you it’s a distraction from your work as architect. Your vision of both macro and micro levels will be greatly enhanced by the time you spend in the belly of the beast bringing it to life.

如果你自己也是项目上的开发，珍惜你写代码的时间，别信任何人说「写代码会分散你作为架构师的精力」。你在野兽肚子里把它激活的过程中花的时间，会极大提升你对宏观和微观两个层面的愿景。

Allison Randal Allison Randal is chief architect and lead developer of the open source project Parrot. In more than 25 years as a programmer, she has developed everything from games to linguistic analysis tools, e-commerce websites, shipping fulfillment, compilers, and database replication systems; worked as a language designer, project manager, conference organizer, editor, and consultant; been president of an open source software foundation; written two books; and founded a tech publishing company.

Allison Randal Allison Randal 是开源项目 Parrot 的首席架构师和首席开发。做了 25 年程序员，她做过从游戏到语言分析工具、电商网站、物流履约、编译器和数据库复制系统的各种东西；当过语言设计师、项目经理、会议组织者、编辑和顾问；担任过开源软件基金会主席；写过两本书；还创办了一家科技出版公司。

12. There Is No One-Size-Fits-All Solution

作者：Randy Stafford

Architects must continuously develop and exercise “contextual sense”— because there is no one-size-fits-all solution to problems that may be widely diverse.

架构师必须持续培养和运用「上下文感知」——因为对千差万别的问题，没有放之四海而皆准的解。

The incisive phrase “contextual sense” was coined, and its meaning insightfully described, by Eberhardt Rechtin in his 1991 book Systems Architecting: Creating & Building Complex Systems (Prentice Hall):

「上下文感知」这个精辟的短语是 Eberhardt Rechtin 1991 年在《Systems Architecting: Creating & Building Complex Systems》（Prentice Hall）一书中提出并深刻阐述的：

[The central ideas of the ‘heuristic approach’ to architecting complex systems] come from asking skilled architects what they do when confronted with highly complex problems. The skilled architect and designer would most likely answer, ‘Just use common sense.’ … [A] better expression than ‘common sense’ is contextual sense—a knowledge of what is reasonable within a given context. Practicing architects through education, experience, and examples accumulate a considerable body of contextual sense by the time they’re entrusted with solving a system-level problem  —typically 10 years.” (emphasis in the original)

「（复杂系统架构的『启发式方法』的核心思想）来自请教有经验的架构师：面对高度复杂的问题时他们怎么做。有经验的架构师和设计师多半会回答：『凭常识就好。』……比『常识』更好的说法是『上下文感知』——在给定上下文里知道什么是合理的知识。执业架构师通过教育、经验和案例，在被委以系统级问题之前（通常要 10 年），积累起相当可观的上下文感知。」（原文强调）

A big problem in the software industry, in my opinion, is that people are often responsible for solving problems requiring more contextual sense than they’ve accumulated. Perhaps this is because the software industry is barely two generations old and growing explosively; perhaps it will be a sign of maturity in the software industry when this problem no longer exists.

在我看来，软件业的一大问题是：人们经常被要求解决需要超过他们已积累上下文感知能力的问题。也许这是因为软件业才两代人历史却在爆炸式增长；也许等这个问题不再存在时，软件业才算成熟。

I encounter examples of this problem frequently in my consulting engagements. Typical examples include failure to apply domain-driven design 1 when appropriate, straying from a pragmatic outlook and over-designing a software solution for the essential need at hand, and making irrelevant or unreasonable suggestions during performance optimization crises.

我在咨询工作中经常遇到这类例子。典型包括：该用领域驱动设计时没用、脱离务实视角对眼前本质需求过度设计、以及在性能优化危机中给出不相关或不合理的建议。

The most important knowledge of software patterns is the knowledge of when to apply them and when not to apply them, and the same is true of different root cause hypotheses and associated corrective actions during problem analysis. In both activities—system architecting and problem analysis — it is axiomatic that there is no one-size-fits-all solution; architects must develop and exercise contextual sense in formulating and troubleshooting their architectures.

软件模式最重要的知识是「什么时候用、什么时候不用」，问题分析中不同根因假设和相应纠正动作也是同理。在这两件事——系统架构和问题分析——里，一条公理就是没有放之四海而皆准的解；架构师必须在设计和排查架构时培养和运用上下文感知。

1 See Eric Evans’s Domain-Driven Design: Tackling Complexity in the Heart of Software (AddisonWesley Professional).

1 参见 Eric Evans《Domain-Driven Design: Tackling Complexity in the Heart of Software》（Addison-Wesley Professional）。

13. It's Never Too Early to Think About Performance

作者：Rebecca Parsons

Business users specify their needs  primarily through functional requirements. The nonfunctional aspects of the systems, like performance, resiliency, up-time, support needs, and the like, are the purview of the architect. However, often the preliminary testing of nonfunctional requirements is left until very late in the development cycle, and is sometimes delegated completely to the operations team. This is a mistake that is made far too often.

业务用户主要通过功能需求来表达需求。系统的非功能方面——性能、弹性、上线时间、支持需求等——是架构师的职责。然而，非功能需求的初步测试经常被拖到开发周期很晚才做，有时甚至完全甩给运维团队。这是个太常见的错误。

The reasons are varied. There is presumably no sense in making something fast and resilient if it doesn’t actually perform the required function. The environments and tests themselves are complex. Perhaps the early versions of the production system will not be as heavily utilized.

原因有几个。如果一个东西根本不实现所需功能，让它快而有弹性大概没意义。环境和测试本身就复杂。也许早期版本的生产系统不会被那么重度使用。

However, if you aren’t looking at performance until late in the project cycle, you have lost an incredible amount of information as to when performance changed. If performance is going to be an important architectural and design criterion, then performance testing should begin as soon as possible. If you are using an Agile methodology based on two-week iterations, I’d say performance testing should be included in the process no later than the third iteration.

然而，如果你直到项目周期很晚才看性能，你已经失去了大量关于「性能什么时候开始掉」的信息。如果性能是重要的架构和设计准则，那性能测试应该尽早开始。如果你用两周迭代的敏捷方法，我会说不晚于第三次迭代就要把性能测试纳入流程。

Why is this so important? The biggest reason is that at the very least you know the kinds of changes that made performance fall off a cliff. Instead of having to think about the entire architecture when you encounter performance problems, you can focus on the most recent changes. Doing performance testing early and often provides you with a narrow range of changes on which to focus.

为什么这这么重要？最大的原因是：至少你知道是哪些改动让性能突然崩盘。遇到性能问题时，你不用去想整个架构，而可以聚焦最近的改动。尽早、频繁地做性能测试，给你一个很窄的改动范围去聚焦。

In early testing, you may not even try to diagnose performance, but you do have a baseline of performance figures to work from. This trend data provides vital information in diagnosing the source of performance issues and resolving them.

早期测试里你甚至可能不试图诊断性能问题，但你有了一份性能数据基线。这些趋势数据在诊断和解决性能问题时提供关键信息。

This approach also allows for the architectural and design choices to be validated against the actual performance requirements. Particularly for systems with stringent requirements, early validation is crucial to delivering the system in a timely fashion.

这种方法还能让架构和设计选择对照实际性能需求做验证。特别是对要求严苛的系统，尽早验证对按时交付至关重要。

Technical testing is also notoriously difficult to get going. Setting up appropriate environments, generating the proper data sets, and defining the necessary test cases all take a lot of time. By addressing performance testing early, you can establish your test environment incrementally, thereby avoiding much more expensive efforts once you discover performance issues.

技术测试也是出了名的难启动。搭合适的环境、造合适的数据集、定义必要的测试用例，都花很多时间。尽早开始性能测试，你可以增量式地搭建测试环境，避免之后发现性能问题时再花大得多的代价。

Rebecca Parsons Dr. Rebecca Parsons is ThoughtWorks’ chief technology officer. She has more than 20 years’ application development experience, in industries ranging from telecommunications to emergent Internet services. Rebecca has published in both language and artificial intelligence publications, served on numerous program committees, and reviews for several journals. She has extensive experience leading in the creation of large-scale distributed object applications and the integration of disparate systems.

Rebecca Parsons Rebecca Parsons 博士是 ThoughtWorks 的首席技术官。她有 20 多年应用开发经验，行业从电信到新兴互联网服务。Rebecca 在语言学和人工智能刊物上都发表过论文，担任过多个程序委员会委员，为几家期刊审稿。她在创建大规模分布式对象应用和异构系统集成方面有丰富的领导经验。

14. Architecting Is About Balancing

作者：Randy Stafford

Balance Stakeholders’ Interests with Technical ­Requirements

在干系人利益与技术需求之间取得平衡

When we think of architecting software, we tend to think first of classical technical activities, like modularizing systems, defining interfaces, allocating responsibility, applying patterns, and optimizing performance. Architects also need to consider security, usability, supportability, release management, and deployment options, among other things. But these technical and procedural issues must be balanced with the needs of stakeholders and their interests. Taking a “stakeholders and interests” approach in requirements analysis is an excellent way to ensure completeness of requirements specifications for the software being developed.

想到软件架构时，我们往往先想到经典技术活动：模块化系统、定义接口、分配职责、应用模式、优化性能。架构师还要考虑安全、可用性、可支持性、发布管理、部署选项等。但这些技术和流程问题必须和干系人需求及其利益取得平衡。在需求分析中采用「干系人与利益」方法，是确保所开发软件需求规格完整性的好办法。

Analyzing the stakeholders and their interests in the process by which an organization develops software, and in the organization itself, reveals the ultimate set of priorities bearing on a software architect. Software architecting is about balancing this set of priorities, over the short and long term, in a way that is appropriate to the context at hand.

分析干系人在组织开发软件过程中的利益、以及对组织本身的利益，能揭示影响软件架构师的最终优先级集合。软件架构就是在短期和长期之间，按当前上下文，平衡这组优先级。

Consider, for example, the engineering department of a software-as-a-service business. The business likely has certain priorities, such as meeting contractual obligations, generating revenue, ensuring customer referenceability, containing costs, and creating valuable technology assets. These business priorities may translate to departmental priorities like ensuring the functionality, correctness,

比如一家 SaaS 公司的工程部。公司可能有这些优先级：履约合同义务、创造收入、确保客户可做 reference、控制成本、创造有价值的技术资产。这些业务优先级可能转化为部门优先级，比如确保所开发软件的功能性、正确性、

and “quality attributes” (i.e., “-ilities”) of the software being developed, as well as ensuring the productivity of the development team, the sustainability and auditability of development operations, and the adaptability and longevity of the software products.

以及「质量属性」（即各种 -ility），同时确保开发团队生产力、开发运营的可持续性和可审计性、软件产品的适应性和寿命。

It is the architect’s job to not only create functional, quality software for users, but also to do so while balancing the other departmental priorities with the cost-containment interests of the business’s CEO, with the easeof-administration interests of the operations staff, with the ease-of-learning and ease-of-maintenance interests of future programming staff, and with the best practices of the software architect’s profession.

架构师的工作不仅是为用户做出功能完整、质量可靠的软件，还要在做这些的同时，把部门其他优先级与 CEO 的成本控制利益、运维人员的易管理性利益、未来程序员的易学易维护利益、以及软件架构师职业的最佳实践平衡起来。

The architect may choose to consciously tilt the balance in favor of one priority in the short term, but had better maintain a proper balance over the long term in order to truly do the job well. And the balance that is struck needs to be appropriate to the context at hand, in consideration of factors such as the expected lifespan of the software, the criticality of the software to the business, and the technological and financial culture of the organization.

架构师可以选择短期有意识地偏向某个优先级，但长期最好保持适当平衡，才能真正把工作做好。而达成的平衡要贴合当前上下文，考虑软件预期寿命、软件对业务的关键性、以及组织的技术和财务文化等因素。

In summary, software architecting is about more than just the classical technical activities; it is about balancing technical requirements with the business requirements of stakeholders in the project.

总之，软件架构不只是经典技术活动；它是在项目中平衡技术需求与干系人的业务需求。

15. Commit-and-Run Is a Crime

作者：Niclas Nilsson

It’s late in the afternoon. The team is churning out the last pieces of the new feature set for the iteration, and you can almost feel the rhythm in the room. John is in a bit of a hurry though. He’s late for a date, but he manages to finish up his code, compile, and check in, and off he goes. A few minutes later, the red light turns on. The build is broken. John didn’t have time to run the automated tests, so he made a commit-and-run and thereby left everybody else hanging. The situation is now changed and the rhythm is lost. Everyone now knows that if they do an update against the version control system, they will get the broken code onto their local machine as well, and since the team has a lot to integrate this afternoon to prepare for the upcoming demo, this is quite a disruption. John effectively put the team flow to a halt because now no integration can be done before someone takes the time to revert his changes.

下午很晚了。团队正在赶本迭代最后几个新功能，房间里几乎能感受到节奏。不过 John 有点赶——他约会要迟到了，但还是写完代码、编译、提交，然后走了。几分钟后，红灯亮了。构建挂了。John 没时间跑自动化测试，于是他「提交就跑」，扔下其他人自己扛。局面变了，节奏没了。现在大家都知道，只要从版本控制 update，就会把坏代码拉到本地，而团队今天下午要做大量集成来准备即将到来的 demo，这一打断相当严重。John 实际上让团队的工作流停了——在有人花时间回滚他的改动之前，谁都没法做集成。

This scenario is way too common. Commit-and-run is a crime because it kills flow. It’s one of the most common ways for a developer to try to save time for himself, and it ends up wasting other people’s time and is downright disrespectful. Still, it happens everywhere. Why? Usually because it takes too long to build the system properly or to run the tests.

这个场景太常见了。提交就跑是犯罪，因为它杀死了心流。这是开发为自己省时间最常见的方式之一，结果浪费了别人的时间，而且相当无礼。但它到处发生。为什么？通常是因为正确构建系统或跑测试要太久。

This is where you, the architect, come into play. If you’ve put a lot of effort into creating a flexible architecture where people can perform, taught the developers agile practices like test-driven development, and set up a continuous integration server, then you also want to nurture a culture where it’s not all right to

这就是你——架构师——登场的地方。如果你已经花大力气搭了让人能发挥的灵活架构、教了开发像测试驱动开发这样的敏捷实践、架了持续集成服务器，那你还想培育一种文化：不允许以任何方式

waste anybody else’s time and flow in any way. To be able to get that, you need to make sure the system, among other things, has a sound architecture for automated testing, since it will change the behavior of the developers. If tests run fast, developers will run them more often, which itself is a good thing, but it also means that they won’t leave their colleagues with broken code. If the tests are dependent on external systems or if they need to hit the database, re-engineer them so they can be run locally with mocks or stubs, or at the very least with an in-memory database, and let the build server run them in the slow way. People should not have to wait for computers, because if they have to, they will take shortcuts, which often causes problems for others instead.

浪费别人的时间和心流。要做到这一点，你需要确保系统——尤其是——有合理的自动化测试架构，因为这会改变开发的行为。如果测试跑得快，开发就会更常跑测试，这本身是好事，也意味着他们不会把坏代码留给同事。如果测试依赖外部系统或要打数据库，就重构它们，让它们能在本地用 mock/stub 跑，或至少用内存数据库跑，让构建服务器去跑慢的那套。人不该等电脑，因为一等，他们就会抄近路，结果往往给别人制造麻烦。

Invest time in making the system fast to work with. It increases flow, lessens the reasons for working in silos, and in the end makes it possible to develop faster. Mock things, create simulators, lessen dependencies, divide the system in smaller modules, or do whatever you have to. Just make sure there’s no reason to even think about doing a commit-and-run.

花时间让系统用起来快。它提升心流、减少各自为战的理由，最终让开发更快。Mock 掉东西、造模拟器、减少依赖、把系统拆成小模块，或者做任何必须做的事。只要确保没人会动念去做「提交就跑」。

Niclas Nilsson Niclas Nilsson is a software development coach, consultant, educator, and writer with a deep passion for the software development craft, and he loves good design and architecture. He is a cofounder of factor10 and the lead editor of the architecture community at InfoQ.

Niclas Nilsson Niclas Nilsson 是软件开发教练、顾问、教育者和作家，对软件开发工艺、好设计和架构有深沉热情。他是 factor10 的联合创始人，也是 InfoQ 架构社区的首席编辑。

16. There Can Be More Than One

作者：Keith Braithwaite

It seems to be a neverending source of surprise and distress to system builders that one data model, one message format, one message transport—in fact, exactly one of any major architectural component, policy, or stance— won’t serve all parts of the business equally well. Of course: an enterprise (“enterprise” is red flag #1) big enough to worry about how many different “Account” tables will impact system building next decade is most likely too big and diverse for one “Account” table to do the job anyway.

系统构建者似乎永远在惊讶和苦恼：一个数据模型、一种消息格式、一种消息传输——事实上，任何主要架构组件、策略或立场，恰好只有一个——不可能同样好地服务业务的所有部分。当然：一个企业（「企业」是红旗 #1）大到要操心未来十年「Account」表会怎么影响系统建设，那它多半太大、太多样，一个「Account」表根本干不完这活。

In technical domains we can force uniqueness. Very convenient for us. In business domains the inconsistent, multifaceted, fuzzy, messy world intrudes. Worse yet, business doesn’t even deal with “the world,” it deals with people’s opinions about aspects of situations in parts of the world. One response is to deem the domain to be technical and apply a unique solution by fiat. But reality has been roughly defined as “that which does not go away when one stops believing in it” (Philip K. Dick), and the messiness always returns as the business evolves. Thus are born enterprise data teams, and so forth, who spend all their (very expensive) time trying to tame existential dread through DTD wrangling. Paying customers tend to find the level of responsiveness that comes from this somewhat unsatisfactory.

在技术领域我们可以强制唯一性。对我们来说很方便。在业务领域，不一致、多面、模糊、混乱的世界闯了进来。更糟的是，业务打交道的甚至不是「世界」本身，而是世界某些部分里人们对情境某些方面的看法。一种应对是宣布这个领域是技术领域，用政令施加唯一解。但现实大致被定义为「当人不再相信它时也不会消失的东西」（Philip K. Dick），而混乱总会随着业务演化卷土重来。于是企业数据团队就诞生了，他们把所有（非常昂贵的）时间花在试图通过扯皮 DTD 来驯服生存焦虑上。付费客户往往觉得这种响应速度不太令人满意。

Why not face up to the reality of a messy world and allow multiple, inconsistent, overlapping representations, services, solutions? As technologists we recoil in horror from this. We imagine terrifying scenarios: inconsistent updates, maintenance overhead, spaghetti-plates of dependencies to manage. But let’s take a hint from the world of data warehousing. The schemata data marts are often (relationally) denormalized, mix imported and calculated values arbitrarily, and present a very different view of the data than the underlying databases. And the sky does not fall because of the nonfunctional properties of a mart. The ETL process sits at the boundary of two very different worlds, typically transaction versus analytical processing. These have very different rates of update and query, very different throughput, different rates of change of design, perhaps very different volumes. This is the key: sufficiently different nonfunctional properties of a subsystem create a boundary across which managing inconsistent representations is tractable.

为什么不正视混乱世界的现实，允许多个、不一致、重叠的表示、服务、方案呢？作为技术人员我们惊恐地后退。我们想象可怕场景：不一致的更新、维护开销、一团乱麻的依赖。但让我们从数据仓库世界取个提示。数据集市的模式经常（关系上）反规范化、随意混合导入值和计算值、呈现和底层数据库非常不同的数据视图。天并没有因为集市的非功能属性而塌下来。ETL 过程坐落在两个非常不同的世界边界上——通常是事务处理和分析处理。它们有非常不同的更新和查询速率、非常不同的吞吐量、不同的设计变更速率，也许体量非常不同。这就是关键：一个子系统足够不同的非功能属性，会创造一个边界，跨这个边界管理不一致的表示是可行的。

Don’t go duplicating representations, or having multiple transports just for the fun of it, but do always consider the possibility that decomposition of your system by nonfunctional parameters may reveal opportunities to allow diverse solutions to your customers’ advantage.

不要仅仅为了好玩就复制表示或搞多个传输方式，但一定要始终考虑这种可能性：按非功能参数分解你的系统，可能会揭示让客户受益的多元解机会。

17. Business Drives

作者：Dave Muirhead

In the context of business enterprise  application development, an architect must act as a bridge between the business and technology communities of an organization, representing and protecting the interests of each party to the other, often mediating between the two, but allowing the business to drive. The business organization’s objectives and operating realities should be the light in which an architect leads technology-oriented decision making.

在企业业务应用开发语境下，架构师必须充当业务和技术两个社区之间的桥梁，互相代表和保护对方利益，经常在两者间调解，但让业务来驱动。业务组织的目标和运营现实，应该是架构师做技术决策时的灯塔。

Businesses routinely plan for and articulate a specific, desired return on investment (ROI) before undertaking a software development initiative. The architect must understand the desired ROI, and by implication, the limits of the value of the software initiative to the business, so as to avoid making technology decisions that could cause the opportunity to be outspent. ROI should serve as a major piece of objective context in the give-and-take conversations with the business about the value of a feature versus the cost of delivering that feature, and with the development team about technical design and implementation. For example, the architect must be careful to represent the interests of the business to the development team by not agreeing to choose technology that has unacceptably costly licensing and support cost implications when the software is deployed into testing or production.

企业在启动软件开发项目前，通常会规划并阐明一个具体的、期望的投资回报率（ROI）。架构师必须理解这个期望 ROI，以及它隐含的该软件项目对业务的价值上限，避免做出让机会被超支的技术决策。ROI 应该作为重要客观背景，在与业务讨论「一个功能值不值交付成本」、与开发团队讨论技术设计和实现时的你来我往中起作用。比如，架构师必须小心向开发团队代表业务利益：不要同意选择那种在测试或生产部署时许可和支持成本高到不可接受的技术。

Part of the challenge of letting the business “drive” is providing enough quality information about the ongoing software development effort back into the business in order to support good business decision making. That’s where transparency becomes crucial. The architect, in conjunction with development management, must create and nurture the means for regular, ongoing information feedback loops. This can be accomplished by a variety of lean

让业务「驱动」的一部分挑战是：要向业务回传足够高质量的软件开发进展信息，以支持好的业务决策。这就是透明度变得关键的地方。架构师要和开发管理层一起，创造并培育定期、持续的信息反馈回路。这可以通过各种精益

software development techniques, such as big visible charts, continuous integration, and frequent releases of working software to the business starting early in the project.

软件开发技术实现，比如大可视化图表、持续集成、以及项目早期就频繁向业务发布可工作的软件。

Software development is fundamentally a design activity, in that it involves an ongoing process of decision making until the developed system goes into production. It is appropriate for software developers to make many decisions, but usually not to make business decisions. However, to the extent that the business community fails to fulfill its responsibility to provide direction, answer questions, and make business decisions for the software development team, it is actually delegating the business decision making to software developers. The architect must provide the macro-context for this ongoing series of microdecisions made by developers, by communicating and protecting the software architecture and business objectives, and must seek to ensure that developers do not make business decisions. Technical decision making untethered to the commitments, expectations, and realities of the business—as articulated by the business community on an ongoing basis—amounts to costly speculation and often results in an unjustifiable expenditure of scarce resources.

软件开发本质上是一种设计活动，因为在开发系统上线前，它是一个持续决策过程。让软件开发做很多决策是合适的，但通常不该让他们做业务决策。然而，如果业务社区没有尽到自己的责任——没有给开发团队指方向、答问题、做业务决策——那实际上就是在把业务决策委托给软件开发。架构师必须为开发这一连串微决策提供宏观背景：沟通和保护软件架构与业务目标，并设法确保开发不做业务决策。脱离业务（由业务社区持续阐明的）承诺、期望和现实的技术决策，等于代价高昂的投机，往往导致对稀缺资源的不合理消耗。

The long-term interests of the software development team are best served when business drives.

软件开发团队的长期利益，在业务驱动时得到最好的保障。

Dave Muirhead Dave Muirhead is a veteran software craftsman and business technologist, and is an owner and principal consultant of Blue River Systems Group, LLC (BRSG), a Denver-based lean software development and technology strategy consulting firm.

Dave Muirhead Dave Muirhead 是资深软件工匠和业务技术专家，也是 Blue River Systems Group, LLC（BRSG）的所有者和首席顾问，这是一家位于丹佛的精益软件开发和技术战略咨询公司。

18. Simplicity Before Generality, Use Before Reuse

作者：Kevlin Henney

A common problem in component frameworks , class libraries, foundation services, and other infrastructure code is that many are designed to be general purpose without reference to concrete applications. This leads to a dizzying array of options and possibilities that are often unused, misused, or just not useful. Most developers work on specific systems: the quest for unbounded generality rarely serves them well (if at all). The best route to generality is through understanding known, specific examples and focusing on their essence to find an essential common solution. Simplicity through experience rather than generality through guesswork.

组件框架、类库、基础服务和其他基础设施代码的一个常见问题是：很多被设计成通用目的，却不参考具体应用。这导致一大堆眼花缭乱的选项和可能性，经常没人用、被误用，或者根本没用。大多数开发做的是具体系统：追求无界通用性对他们没什么好处（如果有的话）。通向通用性的最佳路径是通过理解已知的具体例子、聚焦它们的本质以找到本质的共同解。通过经验获得简单，而不是靠猜测获得通用。

Favoring simplicity before generality acts as a tiebreaker between otherwise equally viable design alternatives. When there are two possible solutions, favor the one that is simpler and based on concrete need rather than the more intricate one that boasts of generality. Of course, it is entirely possible (and more than a little likely) that the simpler solution will turn out to be the more general one in practice. And if that doesn’t turn out to be the case, it will be easier to change the simpler solution to what you now know you need than to change the “general” one that turns out not to be quite general enough in the right way.

在两个本可行的设计之间，「简单先于通用」可以作为打破平局的裁决。有两个可能方案时，选那个更简单、基于具体需求的，而不是那个自称通用的更复杂方案。当然，完全有可能（而且相当有可能）那个更简单的方案在实践中反而是更通用的那个。如果结果不是这样，把一个更简单的方案改成你现在知道需要的样子，也比改那个「通用」结果发现不够通用、而且通用得不对路的方案容易。

Although well meant, many things that are designed just to be general purpose often end up satisfying no purpose. Software components should, first and foremost, be designed for use and to fulfill that use well. Effective generality comes from understanding, and understanding leads to simplification.

虽然出发点好，很多被设计成通用目的的东西，最后往往一个目的也没满足。软件组件首先且最重要的是应该为使用而设计、并且把那个使用做好。有效的通用性来自理解，而理解通向简化。

Generalization can allow us to reduce a problem to something more essential, resulting in an approach that embodies regularity across known examples, a regularity that is crisp, concise, and well grounded. However, too often generalization becomes a work item in itself, pulling in the opposite direction, adding to the complexity rather than reducing it. The pursuit of speculative generality often leads to solutions that are not anchored in the reality of actual development. They are based on assumptions that later turn out to be wrong, offer choices that later turn out not to be useful, and accumulate baggage that becomes difficult or impossible to remove, thereby adding to the accidental complexity developers and future architects must face.

泛化可以让我们把问题约到更本质的东西上，得到一个在已知例子间体现规律的方法——这种规律清晰、简洁、根基扎实。然而太多时候，泛化本身变成了一项工作，把方向拉反了，增加而不是减少复杂度。投机式地追求通用，往往导致方案没有锚定在实际开发的现实上。它们基于后来被证明是错的假设，提供后来被证明没用的选项，积累后来难以或无法卸下的包袱，从而增加开发和未来架构师必须面对的偶然复杂度。

Although many architects value generality, it should not be unconditional. People do not on the whole pay for (or need) generality: they tend to have a specific situation, and it is a solution to that specific situation that has value. We can find generality and flexibility in trying to deliver specific solutions, but if we weigh anchor and forget the specifics too soon, we end up adrift in a sea of nebulous possibilities, a world of tricky configuration options, overburdened (not just overloaded) parameter lists, long-winded interfaces, and notquite-right abstractions. In pursuit of arbitrary flexibility, you can often lose valuable properties—accidental or intended—of alternative, simpler designs.

虽然很多架构师看重通用性，但它不该是无条件的。人们总体上不是为通用性付钱（或需要通用性）：他们有一个具体情境，对那个具体情境的解才有价值。我们可以在试图交付具体解时找到通用性和灵活性，但如果过早抛锚忘记具体，我们最终会漂在模糊可能性的海洋里：一个充满刁钻配置项、超载（不只是重载）参数列表、冗长接口、以及不太对路的抽象的世界。在追求任意灵活性的过程中，你往往会丢掉更简单替代方案的宝贵属性——无论是偶然的还是有意的。

Kevlin Henney Kevlin Henney is an independent consultant and trainer. His work focuses on patterns and architecture, programming techniques and languages, and development process and practice. He is coauthor of A Pattern Language for Distributed Computing and On Patterns and Pattern Languages (both from Wiley).

Kevlin Henney Kevlin Henney 是独立顾问和讲师。他的工作聚焦模式与架构、编程技术与语言、以及开发过程与实践。他合著有《A Pattern Language for Distributed Computing》和《On Patterns and Pattern Languages》（均由 Wiley 出版）。

19. Architects Must Be Hands On

作者：John Davies

A good architect should lead by example. He (or she) should be able to fulfill any of the positions within his team, from wiring the network and configuring the build process to writing the unit tests and running benchmarks. Without a good understanding of the full range of technology, an architect is little more than a project manager. It is perfectly acceptable for team members to have more in-depth knowledge in their specific areas but it’s difficult to imagine how team members can have confidence in their architect if the architect doesn’t understand the technology. As has been said elsewhere, the architect is the interface between the business and the technology team, and thus must understand every aspect of the technology to be able to represent the team to the business without having to constantly refer others. Similarly the architect must understand the business in order to drive the team toward its goal of serving the business.

好架构师应该以身作则。他（或她）应该能干团队里任何位置的活：从接线、配置构建过程，到写单元测试、跑基准测试。如果对全栈技术没有良好理解，架构师不过是个项目经理。团队成员在自己特定领域懂得更深是完全可以接受的，但如果架构师不懂技术，很难想象团队成员怎么会信任他。正如别处说过的，架构师是业务和技术团队之间的接口，因此必须理解技术的方方面面，才能不用老找别人代答就能向业务代表团队。同样，架构师必须理解业务，才能带领团队走向服务业务的目标。

An architect is like an airline pilot: he might not look busy all of the time, but he uses decades of experience to constantly monitor the situation, taking immediate action if he sees or hears something out of the ordinary. The project manager (co-pilot) performs the day-to-day management, leaving the architect free from the hassles of mundane tasks and people management. Ultimately the architect should be responsible for the quality of the projects and their delivery to the business. This is difficult to achieve without authority, which is critical to the success of any project.

架构师像民航飞行员：他可能不一直看起来忙，但他用几十年经验持续监控局面，看到或听到异常就立即行动。项目经理（副驾）做日常管理，把架构师从琐事和人员管理中解放出来。最终架构师应该对项目质量和向业务交付负责。没有权威这很难做到，而权威对任何项目成功都至关重要。

People learn best by watching others; it’s how we learn as children. A good architect should be able to spot a problem, call the team together, and without picking out a victim, explain what the problem is or might be and provide an elegant workaround or solution. It is perfectly respectable for an architect to

人通过观察他人学得最好；我们小时候就是这么学的。好架构师应该能发现问题、把团队叫到一起，不揪出替罪羊，解释问题是什么或可能是什么，并给出优雅的变通或解决方案。架构师向

ask for help from the team. The team should feel it is part of the solution, but the architect should chair the discussion and identify the right solution(s).

团队求助是完全体面的。团队应该觉得自己是解决方案的一部分，但架构师应该主持讨论并确定正确的解。

Architects should be brought into the team at the earliest part of the project; they should not sit in an ivory tower dictating the way forward, but should be on the ground working with the team. Questions about direction or technology choices should not be spun off into separate investigations or new projects, but be made pragmatically through hands-on investigation or using advice from architect peers—all good architects are well connected.

架构师应该在项目最早阶段就加入团队；他们不该坐在象牙塔里指挥方向，而应该在地上和团队一起干。关于方向或技术选择的问题不该被甩出去做独立调查或新项目，而应该通过亲自动手调查或咨询架构师同行来务实地解决——好架构师都是人脉广泛的。

Good architects should be experts in at least one tool of their trade, e.g., an IDE; remember they are hands on. It stands to reason that a software architect should know the IDE, a database architect should know the ER tool, and an information architect should know an XML modelling tool. A technical or enterprise architect, however, should be at least effective with all levels of tooling, from being able to monitor network traffic with Wireshark to modelling a complex financial message in XMLSpy—no level is too low or too high.

好架构师应该精通至少一种本行工具，比如 IDE；记住他们是亲自动手的。顺理成章：软件架构师该懂 IDE，数据架构师该懂 ER 工具，信息架构师该懂 XML 建模工具。而技术或企业架构师应该对各层工具都至少用得动：从用 Wireshark 监控网络流量，到在 XMLSpy 里建模复杂金融报文——没有哪一层太低或太高。

An architect usually comes with a good resume and impressive past. He can usually impress the business and technologists, but unless he can demonstrate his ability to be hands on, it’s difficult to gain the respect of the team, difficult for the team to learn, and almost impossible for team members to deliver what they were originally employed to do.

架构师通常带着漂亮简历和惊艳过往。他通常能打动业务和技术人员，但除非他能展示亲自动手的能力，否则很难赢得团队尊重、团队很难学到东西，团队成员几乎不可能交付他们最初被雇来做的事。

John Davies John Davies is currently chief architect at Revolution Money in the U.S. He recently started a new company called Incept5.

John Davies John Davies 目前是美国 Revolution Money 的首席架构师。他最近创办了一家叫 Incept5 的新公司。

20. Continuously Integrate

作者：David Bartlett

The build as a “big bang” event in project development is dead. The architect, whether an application or enterprise architect, should promote and encourage the use of continuous integration methods and tools for every project.

把构建当作项目开发中「大爆炸」事件的做法已经死了。架构师——无论应用还是企业架构师——应该在每个项目里推动和鼓励使用持续集成方法和工具。

The term continuous integration (CI) was first coined by Martin Fowler in a design pattern. CI refers to a set practices and tools that ensure automatic builds and testing of an application at frequent intervals, usually on an integration server specifically configured for these tasks. The convergence of unit testing practices and tools in conjunction with automated build tools makes CI a must for any software project today.

持续集成（CI）这个术语最早是 Martin Fowler 在一个设计模式里提出的。CI 指一套实践和工具集，确保应用以频繁间隔自动构建和测试，通常在专门为这些任务配置的集成服务器上做。单元测试实践和工具与自动化构建工具的融合，让 CI 成为今天任何软件项目的必备。

Continuous integration targets a universal characteristic of the software development process: the integration point between source code and running application. At this integration point the many pieces of the development effort come together and are tested. You have probably heard the phrase “build early and often,” which was a risk-reduction technique to ensure there were no surprises at this point in development. “Build early and often” has now been replaced by CI, which includes the build but also adds features that improve communication and coordination within the development team.

持续集成瞄准软件开发过程的一个普遍特征：源代码和运行中应用之间的集成点。在这个集成点上，开发工作的各部分汇合并被测试。你大概听过「早构建、勤构建」这句话，它是一种降低风险的技术，确保开发到这个点时不会有意外。「早构建、勤构建」现在已经被 CI 取代，CI 不仅包含构建，还加了改善开发团队内部沟通和协调的特性。

The most prominent part of a CI implementation is the build, which is usually automated. You have the ability to do a manual build, but builds can also be kicked off nightly or can be triggered by source code changes. Once the build is started, the latest version of the source code is pulled from the repository, and the CI tools attempts to build the project and then test it. Lastly, notification is sent out, detailing the results of the build process. These notifications can be sent in various forms including email or instant messages.

CI 实现里最显眼的部分是构建，它通常是自动化的。你可以手动构建，但构建也可以夜间跑，或由源代码变更触发。构建一旦启动，最新版源代码从仓库拉下来，CI 工具试图构建项目然后测试。最后发出通知，详述构建过程结果。这些通知可以通过邮件或即时消息等各种形式发出。

Continuous integration will provide a more stable and directed development effort. As an architect you will love it, but more important, your organization and your development teams will be more effective and efficient.

持续集成会带来更稳定、更有方向的开发工作。作为架构师你会爱上它，但更重要的是，你的组织和开发团队会更有效、更高效。
